title: Power Automate: debug desktop flows using variable default values
summary: The designer steps and roadmap details are supported, but the briefing overstates the absence of administrative controls and makes an unsupported assurance about permissions. Microsoft also documents variable default values contributing to the flow definition stored in Dataverse, so the storage question needs narrowing.

claims.quote: Start execution from a selected action using the variables' default values (Run from here with default values).

claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or environment UI switch or API for this debugging feature is documented.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate desktop flow variable default values API Dataverse workflow clientdata pac powershell; Power Automate desktop "default values" "pac" "PowerShell". Opened manage-variables and developer/desktop-flow-public-apis; no debug-default setter documented.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Sensitive input variable default values are not protected in action modals or the flow definition in Dataverse.
claims.quote: The default values aren't protected in the action modals and the flow definition in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether flow-variable defaults are stored with the flow definition in Dataverse.
claims.quote: The limit applies to the definition of the desktop flow saved in Dataverse, which can't exceed 16M characters. The issue can occur with a large desktop flow, such as when actions have large property values or variables have large default values.
claims.fix: Replace the storage-absence statements with: 'For desktop flows saved in Dataverse using v2 schema, Microsoft documents variable default values as contributing to the stored flow definition.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/schema. Narrow the open question to protection of flow-variable debug defaults when marked sensitive.
